speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly what you feel, such as a spinning sensation, and if the room seems to be moving?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description, Mr. 59; the 3-minute duration of the spinning sensation starting at bedtime is very specific. Did this event occur while you were moving your head, such as rolling over in bed, or was it happening at rest?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the episode lasted only about three minutes and occurred while you were rolling over in bed, did you notice that the spinning stopped completely once you stayed still?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of brief, recurrent spinning vertigo triggered by head position changes (rolling in bed), with spontaneous resolution at rest and no prior history, is highly characteristic of BPPV.
